summary.goal: Polish UX with keyboard navigation, animations, and attention level consistency.

acceptance_criteria.description: Cmd+K / Ctrl+K opens command palette (adapted from planner-ui) searching tree nodes, steps, and projects
Tree crystallizing animation plays when steps first appear (characters resolve from noise to text)
Graduation animation: block shrinks in left column while step appears in right column (coordinated)
Workspace transition animations: columns slide in from edges when navigating between dashboard and project
All components respect the 3-tier attention level system: Level 1 (background, lower weight), Level 2 (foreground, normal weight), Level 3 (raised, card with shadow)
Typography does attention hierarchy — weight and size, not color. Color reserved for semantic meaning only.
Reduced motion respected via prefers-reduced-motion media query

observations: planner-ui already has a CommandPalette component — copy and adapt to search tree nodes + steps + projects (not just plans)
Animations are new: crystallizing (CSS keyframes with text scramble effect), graduation (coordinated Matter.js → CSS transition), workspace transitions (CSS slide)
The attention level system is a cross-cutting pattern — every component already built needs a consistency pass to ensure correct level assignment
Crystallizing animation: characters start as random symbols (@#$%&) and resolve to actual text over ~500ms
Graduation animation: coordinated via shared state — block receives 'graduating' class, triggers CSS shrink, step receives 'appearing' class, triggers CSS slide-in
Workspace transitions: page-level animations when navigating, using view transitions API or CSS transitions
questions: Should command palette show recent items or just search results?
Do we need animation preferences beyond prefers-reduced-motion?
Should attention levels be enforced via TypeScript or just convention?

steps.title: Copy and adapt CommandPalette
steps.description: Copy packages/planner-ui/src/components/CommandPalette.tsx. Adapt search targets: tree nodes (scopes), steps (from current project), projects (from dashboard). Keep Cmd+K / Ctrl+K keyboard shortcut. Use fuzzy search pattern from planner-ui. Navigation: selecting item focuses/zooms to that tree node or navigates to project.

steps.title: Implement tree crystallizing animation
steps.description: Create CSS keyframes for crystallizing effect. Characters start as random symbols (@#$%&*!) and resolve to actual text over 500ms. Apply to steps when first added to tree. Use data-attribute or CSS class to trigger. CSS-only implementation, no JS animation library. Store animation in globals.css.

steps.title: Implement graduation animation
steps.description: Coordinated animation: when block graduates, add 'graduating' class to block (NowColumn) triggering CSS shrink transform. Simultaneously add 'appearing' class to newly created step (ProjectTree) triggering CSS slide-in from left. Duration: 400ms. Use shared state (block_id → step_id mapping) to coordinate timing. CSS transitions, no animation library.

steps.title: Implement workspace transition animations
steps.description: Page-level animations when navigating between dashboard (/) and project (/projects/:id). Columns slide in from edges on enter. Try View Transitions API if browser support allows, fallback to CSS transitions. Use route change detection in React Router. Duration: 300ms. Store transitions in globals.css.

steps.title: Attention level consistency pass
steps.description: Audit ALL components built so far (NowColumn, ProjectTree, ConversationPane, StatusBar, SystemEvent, ContextMarker, StepNode, etc.). Ensure correct attention level assignment: Level 1 (background: system events, timestamps, completed steps — lower weight, subtle), Level 2 (foreground: AI messages, active steps, context markers — normal weight), Level 3 (raised: blocking questions, action items — card with shadow). Typography-driven hierarchy (weight/size), NOT color.

steps.title: Add prefers-reduced-motion support
steps.description: Add @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rules in globals.css. When user has reduced motion preference, disable: crystallizing animation, graduation animation, workspace transitions. Replace with instant state changes or simple fades. Test with macOS accessibility settings.

architect.animation_types: crystallizing (new CSS), graduation (coordinated left→right), workspace transitions (CSS slide)
architect.attention_levels: Level 1 background, Level 2 foreground, Level 3 raised — typography-driven

crystallizing.effect: characters resolve from @#$%& to actual text

graduation.effect: block shrinks in left, step slides in from left in right

workspace_transition.implementation: CSS transitions or View Transitions API

attention_level_rules.level_1: background elements, lower font weight, muted
attention_level_rules.level_3: raised elements, card with shadow, slightly bolder
